locked_decisions: The earlier workflow_api_orchestrations-only design is superseded for operation-level claims; workflow_api_orchestrations remains the workflow-level root and workflow_api_operation_claims is required for operation-scoped claims.

The revised C1-C4 implementation sequence supersedes the earlier C/D sequence; exact replay, approval recovery, and concurrent approval guarantees depend on additive migration 20 and the child-claim table.
Use one provider-neutral durable orchestration root plus operation-level child claims for resumable planning-to-approval API operations.
Keep workflow_api_orchestrations as the workflow-level reservation/root and add workflow_api_operation_claims as the operation-level child boundary.
Each operation claim stores immutable command-plan material, progress, optimistic version, idempotency digest, and final safe response.
Operation claims are unique by tenant, brand, actor reference, operation, and client-key digest; parent workflow reservation uniqueness remains unchanged.
Exact replay returns the stored original response bytes; approval recovery reconciles approval, receipt, evidence, workflow state, and child progress; contradictory state fails closed.

The orchestration root and operation-claim boundary own only durable request claims, server-determined workflow identity references, original canonical subcommand material, progress state and final safe HTTP responses.
Workflow state, approvals, workflow evidence, authorization audit, Campaign Plans and Marketing Briefs retain their existing authorities.
API idempotency remains a completed-response cache; workflow receipts and evidence remain authoritative domain records.

The idempotency key is client-generated and contains at least 128 bits of entropy; raw keys are never logged or returned; implementation validates the accepted representation and length and adds golden tests.
Original canonical subcommand request IDs, timestamps, command kinds, expected versions and safe-command material are persisted before the first authority-changing command.
Concurrent first submissions resolve through a durable uniqueness claim; exact retries reuse original canonical bytes and reconcile only missing steps; changed input conflicts deterministically.
Approval recovery reuses an existing immutable approval and applies only a missing transition.
The customer-facing boundary stops at approved and authorizes no execution or external effect.

Migration 20 is additive, SQLite-canonical, PostgreSQL-compatible, non-cascading, and requires readiness and disposable rehearsal validation; historical migrations remain unchanged and retention/archival remain separately governed.
HTTP contract version, MLAI-CJ-2 envelope schema version 2 and workflow safe-command schema version 1 remain distinct.
Planning-to-approval POST operations retain existing session and CSRF requirements; technical details are omitted for callers without APPROVE.
